<a id="roster"></a>

## Cast

Topic `roster`.

Fields: `roster[].id` (required), `name`, `role`, `aliases`, `view` (`schema.ts` `RosterMember`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readRoster`). `drive` has its own section.

- **What it does.** The characters this story directs. `id` is the story's handle for the character (used by motives, member guidance and macros such as `{{story_role_<id>}}`); `name` is the card name. `role` is one line of what they do in this story; speaker direction and the judge director pick by it, and the judge director runs only when every candidate has a role. `aliases` are other names the player uses ("the captain", a surname); an alias that two members share, or that is another member's name, is ignored. Memory files a character row or a belief about "the captain", "Venn" or "Mara Venn" under the one member those names fit (aliases, the card name, its first or last word, and the member's People page names); a name two members could fit stays as written, and a name memory keeps seeing that fits nobody is listed in Author view's setup list as "same character?" (add an alias to merge, dismiss to keep apart; nothing merges on its own). `view: "omniscient"` makes a narrator see the private rows and aims of the cast so it can foreshadow: always the members on stage, plus, within about 1,000 tokens and most recently named first, the ones the active checkpoint gives a motive or a speaking part and anyone named (by card name, alias or a given name only they carry) in the last 20 messages; the default `own` sees only its own.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "mara", "name": "Mara", "role": "guide who knows the flooded halls: leads the party in and warns of danger", "aliases": ["Mara Venn", "the guide"] }`, and one narrator with `"view": "omniscient"`.
- **Bad.** A roster without roles; the player's own persona in the roster; a card for the role the story gives the player (a greeting that says "You are the lamplighter" and a roster member "The Lamplighter"); two members sharing the alias "the guard".
- **If wrong.** Without roles the judge director falls back and the rules pick the speaker. A role that describes the plot rather than the character steers the wrong person into the scene. A cast member who is the player speaks the player's part and then other characters' lines. Diagnostic `roster-member-is-player` ("Another character speaks as the player: the story casts the player's own role as someone else.") flags a member whose name is the persona, or the role the description, player introduction or a scripted opener gives the player ("you are the …", "the player is a …"); the wizard's agent refuses such a card or member, reading its cards' first messages too. **Wizard cards.** Every card the wizard proposes is checked like the Build a character review: only a missing name, a taken name or an empty description refuse it; everything else (a first message that speaks for the player, a greeting for someone outside the opening scene, an adjective list, a personality whose traits no sentence shows in action ("When X, they do Y"), example blocks without a `{{char}}:` line, a long card, a name SillyTavern would rewrite or that is an everyday word) is a note. A card with notes goes back to the agent once for a revision before you see it, and the notes still left show on the card. After you create a card the wizard reads it back from SillyTavern: if it cannot (or the stored card differs), the card counts as possibly existing, is never created again, and "Check again" retries the read.

<a id="roster-polish"></a>

## Voice and delivery

Topic `roster-polish`.

Fields: `roster[].polish` with `notes`, `prefer`, `avoid`, `tics`, `rhythm`, `by_mood`, `dialogue`, `enabled` (`deliverySchema.ts` `RosterPolish`, `validate/delivery.ts` `readRosterPolish`). Settings: `characters.delivery`, `characters.deliveryRepetition` (install-wide, on by default); the story feature `delivery` (`enabled`, `repetition`) can switch either off for one story.

- **What it does.** A short voice sheet for one cast member. It changes how they word things, never what happens or what they know. Before that character speaks, and only in that character's own private block, the story adds "How you speak (wording only; it never changes what you know, want or do): …" with the `notes` (at most 300 characters: register, sentence habits, what they never say aloud), the `by_mood` line for their current mood (each at most 160 characters, keyed by a value of the member's `mood`, so it needs character life), the `rhythm` (`clipped`, `plain`, `flowing` or `ornate`), "Words that are yours: …" from `prefer` (at most 12, 40 characters each) and "Say it your own way instead of: …" from `avoid` (at most 20). `tics` (at most 12) are model habits you have seen in their replies ("smirks", "a mix of"): nothing bans them, but when one shows in two or more of that character's last six replies it is named back to them. With repetition on (the default, every story, sheet or not) a phrase of three to eight words that a character used in several of their own last six replies is named too: "Lately you keep using: "…" — vary it." (at most three). Replies count for a character only when their speaker name fits exactly one cast member (card name or alias); a narrator's quoted speech counts for nobody. Everything is read from the chat at each draft, so a swipe, edit or delete changes it and nothing is stored. The whole addition stays within about 120 tokens: when it would not, the last `prefer` words go first, then `avoid`, then repeated phrases, then the rhythm, then whole sentences of the notes. `enabled: false` keeps the sheet but switches it (and the repetition line) off for that character. `dialogue` (`keep`, the default, or `voice`) is read only by reply polish. Other characters, the player, the director and every shared memory tier never see a sheet; a sheet line that restates a secret kept from that character is dropped like any other private line.
- **Good.** `{ "notes": "Short sentences. Talks in river terms. Never says sorry out loud.", "prefer": ["current", "mind the rope"], "avoid": ["indeed"], "tics": ["smirks"], "rhythm": "clipped" }`. Record only what the card already shows in its example dialogue (the wizard reads an existing card's first message and example dialogue with `readCharacterCard`); leave a field empty rather than invent a trait.
- **Bad.** A plot fact or a secret in `notes` ("she is the smuggler"); a line about the player ("makes {{user}} nervous"); a name in `avoid` or `tics`; the same word in `prefer` and `avoid`.
- **If wrong.** A name in `tics` or `avoid`, a word in both `prefer` and `avoid`, a cap passed, or `by_mood` without a mood (or with a mood the character does not have) stop the story from loading. Diagnostic `delivery-names-unknown-entity` ("The character is told about someone or somewhere the story has not introduced, and may bring them up early.") flags notes or a mood line naming a codex entry not yet known at the start. Diagnostic `delivery-directs-player` ("A voice note says how this character speaks, never what the player does.") flags a note whose subject is the player. Diagnostic `delivery-over-budget` ("Part of this sheet is left out of the prompt, because the whole addition would pass about 120 tokens.") names what is cut.

<a id="story-polish"></a>

## Reply polish

Topic `story-polish`.

Fields: `polish` with `mode` (`shadow` or `off`) and `narration` (`notes`, `prefer`, `avoid`, `tics`, `rhythm`) (`polishSchema.ts` `StoryPolish`, `validate/polish.ts` `readStoryPolish`); the story feature `polish` (`enabled`, `mode`). Settings: `characters.polish`, `characters.polishMode` (install-wide, on, shadow), `characters.polishMaxPerHour` (40). Role: Reply polish (Connections).

- **What it does.** Polish edits wording, never what happens. After a cast member's reply arrives, and only when code finds a wording problem in it (a word from that member's `avoid`, a `tics` habit seen in two of their last six replies, or a phrase they keep repeating in their own replies), one call to the Reply polish route rewrites only the sentences that hold the problem, in that member's voice sheet (`roster[].polish`, see Voice and delivery). Quoted dialogue and every other sentence stay exactly as written. Code then checks the result: the problem must be gone, and no name, number, negation, "can/will/must", "you", player action, quote, markup or length may change; a held secret or a copied line from the context is refused; any doubt keeps the original. In this build polish runs in `shadow` mode only: it runs and records the result for the author (`chat_metadata.story_orchestrator.polish`, at most 200 rows, rolled back with the chat), and never changes the chat. The automatic rewrite is not built. `mode: "off"` switches it off for this story; the chat's own Features page can override. An `omniscient` narrator uses its own `roster[].polish`, or else the story's `narration` sheet (no `by_mood`). The call sends only that sheet (minus anything naming what the player has not met, and any sentence that would give away a secret), the problems, the reply and the two messages before it; never a card, memory, reasoning, lore or another member's sheet. The Reply polish route defaults to the subscription harness model and never falls back to the play model: with no route nothing is sent. At most `characters.polishMaxPerHour` calls an hour.
- **Good.** `{ "mode": "shadow" }` while you check what polish would change; a narrator's `narration` of `{ "notes": "Present tense. Short paragraphs.", "avoid": ["suddenly"] }`.
- **Bad.** A `narration` sheet with no narrator in the roster; a plot fact or a name in `narration.notes`; expecting polish to fix what a character does (it never repairs behaviour).
- **If wrong.** An unknown `mode` or key, `by_mood` or `dialogue` in `narration`, a name in `narration.avoid` or `tics`, or a `narration` sheet without an `omniscient` member stop the story from loading. A reply polish route that is not answering is the setup row "Reply polish pauses until this model answers again". With another reply post-processor such as Recast running automatically, Setup shows "Two extensions rewrite replies" (`two-polishers`).

<a id="drives-motives"></a>

## Drives and motives

Topic `drives-motives`.

Fields: `roster[].drive`, `checkpoints[].motives` (an object of roster id to text) (`schema.ts`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readMemberText`, `readMotives`).

- **What it does.** A drive is what a character privately wants across the whole story. A motive is what they want at one beat. Both are injected only into that character's private block when they are drafted to speak ("What you want: …", "Right now: …"), and never shown to the player.
- **Good.** Drive: `"bring someone back from the lower halls alive this time"`. Motive at the Ruined Gate: `"size up these strangers and find out whether they would turn back at the first danger"`. One line each, in the character's own interest.
- **Bad.** `"Lead the player to the ruins"` (a plan for the player), `"Be mysterious"` (a stage direction), or a motive keyed `player` or `{{user}}`.
- **If wrong.** A motive for the player's persona is dropped (`motive-for-player`: "The player's choices are theirs, so nobody is told this motive."); a key no cast member has reaches nobody (`motive-member-unknown`). Without motives characters drift: a character with no motive of their own repeats themselves.

<a id="inner-voice"></a>

## Inner voice

Topic `inner-voice`.

Settings: `memory.innerBeat`, `memory.innerFanOut`, `memory.harvestReasoning`, `spikes.thoughtCarry` (install-wide, all on by default; a story's feature policy can switch the inner voice off) (`runtime/coordinators/innerCoordinator.ts`, `runtime/spikes/thoughtCarry.ts`).

- **What it does.** After a character reply the memory model writes a one-line private intent (a beat) for the likely next speaker; a member drafted without one gets a beat at draft time, waited for at most 3 s. With the reasoning harvest on, a reply's reasoning is evidence for that same character's `[intends]` rows. The carried-thought experiment (`spikes.thoughtCarry`) fills the gap when no fresh beat is ready: it takes a standing aim from that character's own reasoning on their latest reply in the current checkpoint (a "goals:" line, or "<name> wants to …"), with no model call. It drops writing instructions and stage directions, first-person lines (the model talking as the writer), lines whose subject is the player under any of their names or another character, and lines that restate a secret the character is kept from. The line reads "Your intent this turn: (carried from your last thought) …", in that character's private block only. It is rebuilt from the chat at every draft, so a swipe, edit or delete changes it and there is nothing to roll back.
- **Good.** Drives and motives authored, so the beat has an aim; a reply model that thinks, so the carry has reasoning to read.
- **Bad.** Counting on the carry for a character whose replies carry no reasoning, or for a narrator whose reasoning is all stage directions (it carries nothing).
- **If wrong.** The journal says why: "Inner beat used", "Inner beat stale", "No inner beat", "Inner thought carried for …", or "No thought to carry for …" with `no-reply`, `no-reasoning` or `no-aim`. Author view only; the player never sees any of it.

<a id="talk-control"></a>

## Speaker direction

Topic `talk-control`.

Field: `checkpoints[].talk_control`: `speakers` `[{ member, weight }]`, `lead`, `no_repeat`, `allow_silence`, `director` (`true` or `{ instruction }`), `chain` (`{ mode, max, sequence, stop_on_transition, stop_on_player, hold_extraction }` or `false`) (`schema.ts` `TalkControl`, `validate/checkpoints.ts` `readTalkControl`).

- **What it does.** Decides who answers in a group while the beat is active (and the chat's "Speaker direction" setting is on). An explicit trigger always wins; then a single name mention; then the director (an AI pick from the candidates, the objective and your `instruction`); then weighted rules (`lead` first, `weight`s, `no_repeat` skips the last speaker). `allow_silence` lets the director hand the turn back to the player. `chain` lets several voices answer one message: `director` mode asks who is next until it hands back, `scripted` mode walks `sequence`; `max` is 1 to 8 (default 3); `stop_on_transition` ends the chain when the story moves.
- **Good.** `{ "lead": "Ruins Narrator", "speakers": [{ "member": "Ruins Narrator", "weight": 3 }, { "member": "Mara", "weight": 2 }], "director": { "instruction": "Pick Ruins Narrator whenever the player acts … Pick Mara when …" } }`. The director reads the instruction and the roles, not the weights, so end the instruction with the scene's real speakers. Chains: 2 at a decision, 4 with `hold_extraction` for an ensemble, `false` for a confession.
- **Bad.** A `lead` left out of `speakers`; an enabled character missing from `speakers`, whom the narrator then voices.
- **Chain repeats.** `no_repeat` defaults on: each member answers at most once in the chain, including a scripted sequence. With no unused member, the chain ends; a repeated scripted entry ends it too. `no_repeat: false` permits repeats up to `max`. A new player line or STOP always ends the old chain, even while its next voice is being chosen.
- **If wrong.** A lead outside the list still joins at weight 1 (`talk-lead-outside-speakers`); a name nobody has falls back to SillyTavern (`talk-member-unknown`); `allow_silence` without the director never happens (`talk-silence-without-director`); a scripted chain without a sequence speaks one voice (`talk-chain-empty`), and an unknown voice in it is skipped (`talk-chain-member-unknown`).

<a id="character-life"></a>

## Character life

Topic `character-life`.

Fields: `roster[].relationships` (`toward`, `axes`, `range`, `step`, `start`, `label`), `roster[].mood` (`baseline`, `values`, `lasts`), `roster[].agenda` (`id`, `goal`, `steps[]` with `text`, `when`, `effect`, `public`, `repeat`; `pace`, `every`), `roster[].schedule` (`when`, `at`) and `clock` (see Story time) (`engine/lifeSchema.ts`, `validate/life.ts`, `engine/life/`).

- **What it does.** Each relationship axis becomes an ordinary int quality `rel_<holder>_<toward>_<axis>` (`toward` is a roster id or `"player"`; `range` defaults to -5 to 5, `start` to 0). It is read while the holder is present and the other side is present or is the player, at most `REL_AXES_PER_READ` (12) of them a read, the speaking character's first; the other characters' pairs take turns, every present pair (all its axes together) at least once every 4 reads while the read's budget holds them. The read never sees the current value and never writes a level: it says whether the window moves the feeling up or down (the extraction read writes `"up"` or `"down"`, the judge picks down, unchanged or up), and the story moves it `step` (default 1) from where it stands, never past the range, whichever model read it. Gates can use it ("trust >= 3 opens the confession"), and a swipe takes it back like any quality. Until the first read the value is `start`: it is on the blackboard from the first turn, so a gate on it sees `start` before anything was read (`start: 2` with a gate `trust >= 2` opens on the first turn), the extractor stays its only writer, and a swipe back past the first read lands on `start` again. `mood` (`values` default calm, tense, angry, afraid, elated) becomes `mood_<id>`, read again after the scene changes (the party `location` or `time_of_day` moved) and falling back to `baseline` after `lasts` (`{boundaries: n}`, or `{until: "scene_break"}`, the default). An `agenda` moves in code at a turn, never by a model: the next step lands when its `when` holds and the pace allows (`per_n_boundaries` every `every` turns, default 3, or once per chapter), and a turn whose player line is out of character (wrapped in `((…))`, or starting `OOC:` / `(OOC`) neither moves it nor counts toward the pace. A landed step's `effect` switches `world_info` (replayed with the path, so a swipe switches it back) and posts `npc_replies` (trigger `onEnter`); an agenda never changes the cast. Only the last step may `repeat`. A `schedule` entry whose `when` holds puts the member at `at`; when that is not the party's `location` (or there is no `location`), the member is dropped from the speaker candidates for that turn, and nothing is written to the group. When the player's latest in-character line speaks to an away member (by name, or by an alias only that member has), that reply's prompt gains one shared line saying the member is not here, so the narrator says so instead of answering for them; a turn that addresses nobody away leaves the prompt as it was. `clock` gives the story a time of day and a day count (see Story time); schedules and mood read `time_of_day` like any quality. The drafted member's private block gains its own feelings ("Your trust toward Arin: 3 on a scale from -5 to 5."), its mood, its last three landed agenda steps and the `public` steps of the others, filtered like every private block so a held secret never reaches a member kept from it. None of it ever reaches a player surface; Author view lists it under Character life.
- **Off-stage events.** When the story moves on or a scene ends, the memory model proposes one short off-stage event per member with an `agenda`, kept inside that member's plan (Story → Features › Off-stage events). By default each one applies on its own (`stagecraft.meanwhileAcceptMode` `auto`); set Review and each waits for you in Author view, set Off and none are proposed. An applied event lands at a boundary, reaches only that member's private block at the next reply, and a swipe of the message takes it back.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "arin", "relationships": [{ "toward": "player", "axes": ["trust"], "range": [-3, 3] }], "mood": { "baseline": "calm" }, "agenda": [{ "id": "debt", "goal": "Repay the smuggler before the festival", "pace": "per_n_boundaries", "every": 4, "steps": [{ "text": "sold her mother's ring" }, { "text": "met the smuggler at the docks", "when": { "q": "location", "op": "!=", "v": "docks" } }] }], "schedule": [{ "when": { "q": "time_of_day", "op": "==", "v": "night" }, "at": "the docks" }] }`.
- **Bad.** `display` on a `rel_*` quality (refused: feelings are never public); an agenda step with `cast_changes` (refused: use a checkpoint); `pace: "per_chapter"` in a story without `chapters` (refused, `agenda-pace-no-chapters`: it would move once and never again; use `per_n_boundaries` with `every`, or add chapters); a relationship toward the member itself or toward an id not in the roster (refused); an authored quality named like a compiled one (refused).
- **If wrong.** Too many axes in one scene: the rest are left out of that read and Author view's setup list names them (`relationship-scope-overflow`); in a crowded scene a pair can wait longer than 4 reads.

<a id="factions"></a>

## Factions and standing

Topic `factions`.

Fields: `factions[]` (`id`, `name`, `range`, `start`, `bands`, `visible_when`, `introduce`, `moves[]` with `id`, `when`, `add`, `heard_by`) and `roster[].factions` (`engine/factionSchema.ts`, `validate/factions.ts`, `engine/factions/standing.ts`).

- **What it does.** A faction is a group such as a guild, a village or the crown. Its standing with the player is an ordinary int quality `rep_<id>` (`range` default -5 to 5, `start` default 0), on the blackboard from the first turn. It moves only on story events: a `move` fires once ever, the first turn its `when` holds (after quest rewards, and again after a transition), adding `add` (clamped to the range), and its record `rep_<id>_move_<move>` keeps the turn it fired; a quest `reward.set {"rep_<id>": {"add": n}}` moves it too. It never moves on time or on what the player did not do, and a checkpoint `state_snapshot` never writes it (a `rep_*` key there is the warning `faction-snapshot-key`). A member listed in `roster[].factions` (at most 3) hears a move when it is present that turn (`heard_by: "present"`, the default: not away by its schedule and not switched off in the group) or always (`heard_by: "faction"`), and keeps its own `rep_<id>_seen_<member>`. A drafted member gets one private line per faction: "Your group, The Guild, regards the player as: Wary (as far as you have heard). Let it colour how you open toward them; your own feelings come first." The player sees the band word of a faction whose `visible_when` holds (default: always) in a Standing group on the Stat sheet and in `roster` rows with `faction`, never a number, a range or an arrow. The living director gets the band of each visible faction; a hidden one reaches it only with `introduce: true`, and then by name alone. A swipe takes standing, what members heard and the move records back. Author view lists each faction under Factions: its number, band, members and the moves that fired.
- **Good.** `{ "factions": [{ "id": "guild", "name": "The Guild", "bands": [{ "max": -3, "label": "Hostile" }, { "max": -1, "label": "Wary" }, { "max": 2, "label": "Neutral" }, { "label": "Trusted" }], "visible_when": { "q": "met_guild", "op": "==", "v": true }, "moves": [{ "id": "saved-apprentice", "when": { "q": "apprentice_saved", "op": "==", "v": true }, "add": 2, "heard_by": "faction" }, { "id": "stole-ledger", "when": { "q": "ledger_stolen", "op": "==", "v": true }, "add": -2 }] }], "roster": [{ "id": "mara", "factions": ["guild"] }] }`. Three to five bands; finer bands give the number away.
- **Bad.** A move that lowers standing on inaction (refused, `faction-move-on-inaction`): a `not` at the top of its gate, a gate that reads only time (`message_count`, `story_day`, …), or a leaf that holds before anything happens (`== false`, `!= true`, or the quality's start value); a move whose gate holds at the start (refused); `display` on a `rep_*` quality or an authored `rep_*` quality (refused); a reward that writes `rep_<id>_seen_*` or a move record (refused); an id with an underscore (refused).
- **If wrong.** A faction with no move and no reward never changes (`faction-never-moves`); with `display.standing: false` and no roster row the player never sees it (`faction-no-visible-band`). A move gate the reader is never asked about stays false: move gates are read a few at a time, in rotation, and Author view names the ones left out of a read.

<a id="rumors"></a>

## Rumors and gossip

Topic `rumors`.

Fields: `rumors[]` (`id`, `from`, `claim`, `about`, `versions[]` with `text`, `truth`, `weight`; `starts_when`, `leaks_to[]` with `member`, `when`) and `roster[].gossip` (`talks_to`, `contact`, `when`, `delay` with `boundaries` or `days`, `hops`) (`engine/rumorSchema.ts`, `validate/rumors.ts`, `memory/rumors/spread.ts`, `runtime/rumorPort.ts`).

- **What it does.** A rumor is news that moves between characters over story time. It starts with `from` the first turn its `starts_when` holds (or the first turn, without one). A member's `gossip` says whom it passes news to (`talks_to`, one way), when (`when`, a gate, optional) and how it reaches them: `contact: "together"` (the default) needs both members' schedules to put them in the same place, `"any"` reaches them anywhere (letters, messengers), a gate is your own rule. After a delay (`delay.boundaries: [min, max]` turns, default 1 to 3, or `delay.days` with a story clock) the receiver hears it, and passes it on to its own `talks_to`, up to `hops` (default 2, at most 3) steps from the start. Each hop picks one of the `versions` by `weight`, so a rumor may change on the way; `truth` is for you alone and never reaches a prompt or the player. The receiver gets a private line, "Bryn told you: the mill burned down (you are not sure of it; hearsay, it may be wrong)": whether it believes the teller follows its relationship toward them (the first axis in its top third believes, bottom third doubts, else not sure). It is hearsay, not knowledge: the reader never turns a repeated rumor into a fact. The player meets a rumor only when a character repeats it. Everything is code: no model call, the same chat always draws the same delays and versions, at most 3 hops land a turn, a member outside the group never sends or receives, and a swipe or edit takes a landed hop back to pending (it lands again at the same point). Author view lists every hop under Memory › Rumors.
- **Secrets.** A rumor never carries a secret kept from someone: a hop whose words restate a secret that member is kept from waits and never lands. A `leaks_to` row lets it out to one member when its `when` holds: that member, and only that member, now knows the secret; every other member it is kept from is still kept from it.
- **Good.** `{ "rumors": [{ "id": "mill-fire", "from": "bryn", "claim": "the old mill burned down", "versions": [{ "text": "the old mill burned down", "truth": "true", "weight": 3 }, { "text": "someone set the old mill on fire", "truth": "false", "weight": 1 }], "starts_when": { "q": "mill_burned", "op": "==", "v": true } }], "roster": [{ "id": "bryn", "gossip": { "talks_to": ["tam"], "contact": "any", "delay": { "boundaries": [1, 2] } } }] }`.
- **Bad.** A rumor whose words restate a secret relationship label (refused: a secret reaches one person through `leaks_to`); a member who passes news to itself, an unknown member, `delay.days` without a clock, `hops` above 3 (refused).
- **If wrong.** A rumor that never moves: check `contact` (two members never in the same place never meet) and that the receivers are enabled in the group.

<a id="relationship-labels"></a>

## Relationship labels

Topic `relationship-labels`.

Fields: `roster[].relationships[].public` (`label`, `when`, `follows_feeling`, `hold`) and `roster[].relationships[].secret` (`id`, `label`, `revealed_when`) (`engine/lifeSchema.ts`, `validate/life.ts`, `engine/life/labels.ts`, `runtime/labelView.ts`).

- **What it does.** A relationship can carry words the player sees, never its number. `public` rows say how the holder visibly treats the other side ("wary", "warming to you"): the last row whose `when` holds (or that has no `when`) is shown, in the present tense, at most 6 rows of plain text up to 40 characters. `secret` rows (at most 4) stay out of every player surface until `revealed_when` holds once; that turn latches `life_reveal_<holder>_<toward>_<id>` (the turn it was learned), and the secret stays learned for good: a later change never un-reveals it, only a swipe, edit or delete of the reply that earned it does. A learned secret reads as history ("Learned: secretly loyal to you"), never as a present claim. Labels show on the holder's People page in the Journal (a page is added for a holder without a codex entry) while both the holder and the other side are known to the player (a cast member enabled in the group, or one whose People entry is known; the player always is); a row toward someone the player has not met is absent. A reveal adds a log row and a "Revealed" chip under the message that earned it. The holder's private line names its labels ("shown as: wary; secretly: loyal, which others have not learned", or "which the player now knows"); no other member, no shared prompt and the director ever get a secret, and a reveal to the player is not a reveal to the cast. The story reads every key a label gate names (in the same rotation as People and Places), except feeling keys, which the feelings read already asks. Author view lists each label with its gate and when a secret was learned (turn and message), and a "why this number" list under each feeling: every step with its turn, message and the evidence that moved it. A step whose evidence repeats the cause of the last step on the same feeling within 4 turns is held ("same beat"), so a lingering mood moves a feeling once.
- **Follows the feeling.** A public row whose `when` reads a `rel_*` feeling is a word band over the hidden number, and the player can read its movement from it: it needs `follows_feeling: true` (else refused), and may set `hold` (1 to 5 turns its gate must hold before the label switches) against flicker. Prefer event gates.
- **Good.** `{ "toward": "player", "axes": ["trust"], "public": [{ "label": "wary" }, { "label": "trusts your discretion", "when": { "q": "kept_secret", "op": "==", "v": true } }], "secret": [{ "id": "loyal", "label": "secretly loyal to you", "revealed_when": { "q": "saw_letter", "op": "==", "v": true } }] }`.
- **Bad.** A public label that names the secret ("cold, but secretly loyal": `relationship-secret-in-public`, the player knows it before the reveal); a secret revealed by a feeling's number (`relationship-label-reads-axis`: the reveal tells the player the number moved); a label naming someone the player has not met (`disclosure-names-unknown-entity`); a secret whose gate holds at the start or whose text equals a public label (refused).
- **If wrong.** A label gate nobody reads stays false; label gates ride the codex rotation, so a crowded read asks them a turn later.

<a id="commitments"></a>

## Promises to the player

Topic `commitments`.

Fields: `roster[].commitments[]` (`id`, `what`, `made_when`, `kept_when`, `broken_when`, `due`, `heard`, `effect`) (`engine/lifeSchema.ts`, `validate/commitments.ts`, `engine/life/commitments.ts`, `runtime/commitmentView.ts`).

- **What it does.** A cast member can promise the player something ("repay the debt from the river"), and the story remembers it on the member, the holder. A commitment is made the first turn `made_when` holds (or is open from the start with `"start"`), then kept the first turn `kept_when` holds, or broken the first turn `broken_when` holds; each step latches `life_commit_<member>_<id>_made`, `_kept` or `_broken` (the turn it happened) and stays, and only a swipe, edit or delete of the reply that earned it takes it back. When both hold in one turn, kept wins. While it is open the holder's private block carries "You told the player you would <what>. It is not done yet; it is yours to keep, raise or explain.", and adds "It is overdue." once `due` has passed (`{"boundaries": n}` turns after it was made, or `{"story_day": d}` with a story clock) or, without `due`, after 12 turns; overdue is never broken. The turn it is kept, the holder reads "You kept your word to the player: <what>." once; the turn it is broken, "You did not keep your word to the player: <what>." once. No other member, no shared prompt and no player surface gets the holder's line. The player sees "Promised you: <what> (open)", then "(kept)" or "(broken)", on the holder's People page in the Journal (a page is added for a holder without a codex entry) while the holder is known; `heard: false` keeps a promise made out of the player's hearing off every player surface, for a twist. There is no countdown, no overdue marker and no reminder for the player, and the player owes nothing because a character offered something. The living director gets each open, heard promise of a member who is not away as a hook ("Mara has promised the player to ..."). A kept promise may carry an `effect` (`world_info`, replayed from the latch so a swipe switches it back, and `npc_replies` with trigger `onEnter`). The story reads the keys of the gates a promise waits on, in the same rotation as People and Places. Author view lists each promise under Character life with its state, the turn and whether it is overdue. At most 6 a member; `what` is plain text up to 160 characters.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "mara", "commitments": [{ "id": "gate", "what": "get past the north gate together", "made_when": { "q": "mara_offered_help", "op": "==", "v": true }, "kept_when": { "q": "past_north_gate", "op": "==", "v": true }, "broken_when": { "q": "mara_betrayed_party", "op": "==", "v": true }, "due": { "boundaries": 8 } }] }`. Write `what` as a verb phrase both sides read: the holder sees "You told the player you would get past the north gate together", the player sees "Promised you: get past the north gate together".
- **Bad.** A `broken_when` that holds by waiting or absence (refused, `commitment-broken-on-inaction`): a `not` at the top, a gate that reads only time (`message_count`, `story_day`, ...), or a leaf that holds before anything happens (`== false`, `!= true`, the quality's start value); a `kept_when` that holds at the start, `due.story_day` without a clock, an id with an underscore or a promise to anyone but the player (refused: between members use an agenda); "you", "I" or "me" in `what` (`commitment-what-names-a-side`: one side reads it wrong).
- **If wrong.** A promise that never resolves: its keys are read a few at a time, so a crowded read asks them a turn later; check that some story event can set `kept_when`.

<a id="cues"></a>

## Remarks and reactions

Topic `cues`.

Fields: `roster[].cues[]` (`id`, `kind`, `when`, `cue`, `lane`, `priority`, `window`, `repeat`, `landed_when`, `max_offers`) (`engine/cueSchema.ts`, `validate/cues.ts`, `engine/life/cues.ts`, `engine/life/offers.ts`, `runtime/cuePort.ts`).

- **What it does.** A cast member can notice specific things. A `remark` is offered while its `when` holds ("in the market while the guild is angry"); a `reaction` answers an event: the first turn its `when` holds latches `cue_<member>_<id>_at`, and the cue is offered for `window` turns from there (default 3). When the member is drafted to reply, the story picks at most one cue for it and puts one line in that member's private block: "If it fits, you may react to: <cue>. React as yourself; the player's actions and feelings are theirs." It is a suggestion the model voices in character, never a posted message, never the player's act, never mandatory speech. Only the drafted member ever sees it; the line is checked against every secret kept from that member at each generation and dropped if it would restate one (an omniscient narrator's line must also pass the player's view and name only people and places the player knows). A cue counts as offered only when the line reached that generation's prompt and the member answered with a real reply; a swipe or edit of that reply takes the offer back, so the next reply is offered the same cue again.
- **Lanes and order.** `lane: "may"` (default) is spent once offered, or with `repeat: {"cooldown": n}` may come back after n turns; two may cues of one member are at least 2 turns apart. `lane: "must"` is for something story-critical: it is offered again on later replies, at most `max_offers` times (default 3, at most 5), until `landed_when` holds after an offer, which latches `cue_<member>_<id>_landed` (a gate can read it). An offer made by the reply that commits a turn counts from the next turn. The pick: must before may, then higher `priority` (default 0), then the kind (a raised topic, then an echo, then a norm, then a cue), then declaration order. Nothing is drawn at random. Write a broad cue at priority 0 and specific ones above it; the gate is where arc state belongs (a broad default with specific overrides, kept to the one story graph). Author view lists each cue under Character life with its offers, when a reaction latched, whether a must cue landed, which cue the member's next reply would get, what ties with it and why others are held; journal rows "cue offered", "cue landed", "cue not landed" and "offer lapsed" record the rest. An unlanded cue is not a fault: Repair stays silent.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "mara", "cues": [{ "id": "ledger", "kind": "reaction", "when": { "q": "ledger_returned", "op": "==", "v": true }, "cue": "the stolen ledger is back in the guild's hands" }, { "id": "warn", "kind": "remark", "lane": "must", "when": { "q": "guild_angry", "op": "==", "v": true }, "cue": "the guild is hunting whoever took the ledger", "landed_when": { "q": "heard_warning", "op": "==", "v": true } }] }`.
- **Bad.** A reaction whose `when` holds by waiting or absence (refused, `cue-needs-event`: a `not` at the top, a gate that reads only time, or a leaf that holds before anything happens); a must cue without `landed_when`, `landed_when` or `max_offers` on a may cue, `window` on a remark, an id with an underscore, an authored quality named `cue_*` or `topic_*` in a story with cues (refused); two cues of one member with the same lane and priority (`cue-tie`: declaration order decides); a cue that says what the player does or feels (`cue-narrates-player`).
- **If wrong.** A reaction that never offers: its gate keys are read a few at a time with People and Places, so a crowded read asks them a turn later; check the member is enabled and not away when it replies. A must cue that never lands: `landed_when` needs an event the story can read after the member has spoken.

<a id="topics"></a>

## Topics a character deepens

Topic `topics`.

Fields: `roster[].topics[]` (`id`, `keys`, `tiers[]` with `cue`, `when`; `priority`) (`engine/cueSchema.ts`, `validate/cues.ts`, `engine/life/cues.ts`, `talk/directAddress.ts`).

- **What it does.** A topic is a subject the player can raise with one member, up to three tiers deep. A raise happens only when the player's latest in-character line addresses that member by name in the player's own words, as a vocative ("Mara, what about the ledger?" or "What about the ledger, Mara?"), addresses no one else, and names one of `keys` as a whole term. The member is then offered the next tier through the same one-cue channel ("The player asked you about this directly. If it fits, you may tell them: <tier>."), at priority 30 by default, so a raised topic outranks a waiting echo or norm but never a must cue. Each answered raise steps `topic_<member>_<id>` once (at most once per player line); a tier with `when` waits until it holds, and the topic stays at the previous tier meanwhile, so asking again never unlocks a tier the story gated. A name in narration (`*I glance at Mara*`), a third-person mention ("I saw Mara at the docks"), an out-of-character line, a key said anywhere else in the chat, or a line that addresses two members never counts. If a must cue wins that reply, the raise is not used up and the member's next reply to the same line can still take it; a swipe or regenerate of the answer offers the same tier again; an edit of the player's line is a new raise. When the player's speech is in quotes, only the quoted words count as addressing.
- **Good.** `{ "id": "mara", "topics": [{ "id": "ledger", "keys": ["ledger", "accounts"], "tiers": [{ "cue": "the ledger lists debts the guild never paid" }, { "cue": "the last page names the magistrate", "when": { "q": "trusts_player", "op": "==", "v": true } }] }] }`.
- **Bad.** A key that is a cast member's name or alias (refused: the key is the subject, never who is asked); more than 3 tiers or 8 keys (refused); two or more tiers with no `when` (`topic-ungated-depth`: asking alone reaches the deepest tier).
- **If wrong.** A raise that never registers: write the member's card name or a distinct alias at the start or end of the spoken clause, followed by a comma or question mark.

<a id="norms"></a>

## Social norms

Topic `norms`.

Fields: `norms[]` (`id`, `label`, `broken_when`, `noticed_by`, `cue`, `priority`, `checkpoints`) (`engine/cueSchema.ts`, `validate/cues.ts`, `engine/life/cues.ts`).

- **What it does.** A norm is a social rule the cast holds ("guests do not draw steel at the table"); `label` is for you only. The first turn `broken_when` holds (only at the listed `checkpoints`, when given) latches `cue_norm_<id>_at`, and `cue_norm_<id>_<member>_at` for each member of `noticed_by` who is not away then. Each such witness is offered `cue` as a reaction for 3 turns, at priority 15 by default, through the same one-cue channel. Who saw it is what you list: the story does not guess. A norm keeps no score and changes no standing; a story that wants consequences gates on `cue_norm_*` or uses a faction move.
- **Good.** `{ "norms": [{ "id": "steel", "label": "no drawn steel at the host's table", "broken_when": { "q": "drew_weapon_at_feast", "op": "==", "v": true }, "noticed_by": ["mara", "host"], "cue": "a guest drew steel at the host's table" }] }`.
- **Bad.** A `broken_when` that holds by waiting or absence (refused, `cue-needs-event`); an unknown member or checkpoint (refused); a cue that says what the player feels (`cue-narrates-player`).
- **If wrong.** A witness who never reacts: it was away when the norm broke, or not enabled in the group when it replied within the 3 turns (Author view shows the lapse and its reason).

<a id="echoes"></a>

## Delayed echoes

Topic `echoes`.

Fields: `echoes[]` (`id`, `after` with `transition`, or `quest` and `to`, or `milestone`, or `check` and `outcome`; `delay` with `parts` or `boundaries`; `when`, `cancel_when`, `expires`, `to`, `cue`, `hold`) (`engine/echoSchema.ts`, `validate/echoes.ts`, `engine/life/echoes.ts`, `runtime/echoPort.ts`).

- **What it does.** An echo is a consequence that comes back later: "when this happened, then after a while, if the world still supports it, tell this character this". `after` names one event: a transition (`"from->to"`, with `#1` for a second transition between the same two checkpoints), a quest ending (`to: "done"` or `"failed"`), a milestone earned, or a check result (`outcome`: success, failure, miss, weak or strong). The turn it happens schedules the echo, with a delay drawn once for the chat from `delay`: `{"boundaries": [min, max]}` turns (at least one turn later) or `{"parts": [min, max]}` day parts of story time (needs a `clock`). When the delay has passed the echo checks again, every turn until it lands: `when` must hold (optional), the recipient must be enabled in the group, and the cue must not restate a secret kept from its audience. `to` is a cast id, or `"narrator"` for the cast member with `view: "omniscient"`; a narrator's reply is read by the player, so its cue must also keep the player's secrets and name only people and places the player has met. While it waits it may still expire: past `expires` (default 6 turns, or 4 day parts, counted from when it was due, in the delay's unit) it is dropped, even when a time skip crosses both points in one turn. `cancel_when` drops it at any turn before it lands. At most 2 echoes land a turn; the rest wait, and their expiry keeps counting. A landed echo is handed to the same one-cue channel as reactive cues, at priority 20 (below a raised topic and any must cue, above norms and remarks), for `hold` turns (default 2, at most 6), as a bullet under "Coming back now, already decided by earlier events (bring it into this reply through the world or the people in it; never decide what the player does, says or feels):". It counts as offered only when that cue reached the reply's prompt and the member answered; unused by the end of `hold`, it lapses. Each echo happens at most once in a chat: a later repeat of its event never schedules it again, whether it landed, lapsed, expired or was cancelled. Nothing is drawn at random beyond the seeded delay, there is no model call, echoes never move story time and write nothing a gate can read. A swipe, edit or delete takes back what that reply led to (the schedule, a landing, a cancel or expiry), and replaying it gives the same result. Author view lists each echo under Memory › Echoes with its state (scheduled, due, waiting and why, landed to channel, offered, cancelled, expired, lapsed), its source and any turns the story could not scan (an echo added to a long chat cannot see events older than the kept history). Journal author rows record schedules, landings and endings.
- **Good.** `{ "echoes": [{ "id": "trader-returns", "after": { "transition": "market->road" }, "delay": { "parts": [2, 4] }, "when": { "q": "trader_repaid", "op": "==", "v": false }, "cancel_when": { "q": "trader_repaid", "op": "==", "v": true }, "to": "narrator", "cue": "the trader the player short-changed is in town and remembers" }] }`.
- **Bad.** A delay in `parts` without a clock, an unknown transition, quest, milestone or check, an outcome a check never gives, `to` outside the cast, `"narrator"` with no omniscient member, `expires` in a different unit from the delay, `hold` above 6 or a second echo with the same id (refused); a cue that says what the player does or feels (`echo-speaks-for-player`); a cue naming someone or somewhere the player may not have met when it lands (`echo-names-unknown-entity`: it waits and may expire); a `cancel_when` that already holds at the start (`echo-gate-holds-never`: it is cancelled before it can land).
- **If wrong.** An echo that never lands: check Author view's reason; a member who is never enabled, or a `when` the story never makes true, lets it expire. An echo in a story you updated keeps what it already did; an edited gate or delay reschedules a pending echo from the kept history, an edited cue alone lands with the new words.

<a id="story-time"></a>

## Story time

Topic `story-time`.

Fields: `clock` (`times`, `start_day`, `start_part`, `night`, `max_skip_days`), `calendar` (`start` with `year`, `month`, `day`, `weekday`; `months[]` with `name`, `days`; `weekdays`, `seasons[]` with `name`, `from_month`; `label`) and `checkpoints[].effects.time` (`advance` with `days`, `parts`; `to` with `part`, `next_day`), compiled to `story_time`, `story_day`, `time_of_day`, `time_part`, `is_night` and `cal_*` (`engine/lifeSchema.ts`, `validate/life.ts`, `engine/life/clock.ts`, `engine/life/calendar.ts`).

- **What it does.** `clock.times` names the parts of a day in order (at least two, such as morning, afternoon, evening, night). The story keeps one number, `story_time`: the parts of a day passed since the story began, starting at `(start_day - 1) × parts + start_part` (`start_day` default 1, `start_part` default the first time). Everything else is worked out from it at every turn and cannot be written: `story_day` (day 1, 2, …), `time_of_day` (the part's name), `time_part` (0 for the first part), `is_night` (true while the part is one of `clock.night`, default none) and, with a `calendar`, `cal_year`, `cal_month`, `cal_day_of_month`, `cal_weekday` and `cal_season`. Time never comes from the wall clock. Three things move it, always forward: the reader, which names the part of day the window shows and moves the clock at most one part a turn (until the first read or move, an unanchored clock with no `start_part` takes the part the reader names on day 1); a checkpoint's `effects.time` when the story enters it (`{"advance": {"days": 2}}`, or `{"to": {"part": "morning", "next_day": true}}`: a later part today moves to it, the same part only with `next_day`, an earlier part means tomorrow), at most `clock.max_skip_days` (default 30) at once; and the author (`/cp set time_of_day night` moves forward to the next night). A read of messages from before a checkpoint or author move is out of date and moves nothing. `calendar.start` is the date of story day 1 (`month` is a month name or its number from 1; `weekday` a weekday name or its index from 0, default the first); `start_day` only moves where the story begins in it. Seasons start at `from_month` and run to the next; months before the first season belong to the last. `label` (`date` default, or `day`) is how the time is written: "3rd of Thawmonth, morning" or "Day 4, morning". A swipe takes time back with the reply that moved it; a reopened chat keeps it. A `timeline` stop without an authored date shows the time the chat first reached it. Gates may read every time key: a deadline is an ordinary `failed_when` on `story_day`. Author view shows the time and what last moved it under Character life. The player sees time only where a timeline shows it.
- **Good.** `"clock": { "times": ["morning", "afternoon", "evening", "night"], "night": ["night"], "start_part": "evening" }`, `"calendar": { "start": { "year": 412, "month": "Thawmonth", "day": 27, "weekday": "Starday" }, "months": [{ "name": "Deepwinter", "days": 31 }, { "name": "Thawmonth", "days": 28 }], "weekdays": ["Moonday", "Starday", "Fireday"], "seasons": [{ "name": "Spring", "from_month": "Thawmonth" }] }`, and on the checkpoint after a journey `"effects": { "time": { "advance": { "days": 3 } } }`.
- **Bad.** `effects.time` on the start checkpoint (refused: use `start_day` and `start_part`), without a clock (refused), with a negative or empty advance, an unknown part or more than `max_skip_days` (refused); a `calendar` without a `clock` (refused); an authored quality named `story_time`, `time_part`, `is_night`, `cal_*` or `time_reached_*` (refused); a quest `reward.set` on a time key (refused: time moves by the clock); an offered quest whose `failed_when` reads only time (refused, see Quests).
- **If wrong.** Time stands still when nothing reads it: the reader is asked about the time of day only while a gate the story is waiting on names a time key, so a story whose time matters for schedules alone should move it with `effects.time`. `elapsed` is real seconds, not story time; use `story_time` for anything in the fiction.

<a id="living-cards"></a>

## Living cards

Topic `living-cards`.

Fields: `roster[].card` and `player.card` (`fields`, each `{quality, visual}`), and `checkpoints[].effects.card` (`{owner: {field: value}}`) (`engine/cardFields.ts`, `runtime/cardLedger.ts`).

- **What it does.** A card field is a part of a character's look or description that can change in one chat without touching the card itself: `"card": {"fields": {"hair": {"quality": "arin_hair", "visual": true}}}`. Each field binds one quality, which must be a non-latching, non-monotonic extractor `string` or `enum` (a quality binds to one field at most, a card declares at most 64, a field id is a lowercase word). The reader keeps the quality current from the chat like any other ("Arin dyes her hair red" moves it), so the change stays in this chat's story state, a swipe takes it back, and a new chat starts from the card as written. `visual: true` sends the field to pictures and sprites as part of the look. A checkpoint can set a field when it starts: `"effects": {"card": {"arin": {"hair": "red"}}}` names an owner (a roster id, or `player`), a declared field and a short value the quality allows (240 characters at most). Author view lists the current values and who wrote each (the reader, the checkpoint, or the author). A placeholder such as "unknown", "none", "n/a" or "unchanged" is never written to a card field: the field keeps its value, so a read that does not know the outfit renders nothing new.
- **Good.** One field per thing that really changes in the story (hair, a scar, a uniform), each with a rubric that says what to look for; `visual` only on what a picture should show.
- **Bad.** A field bound to a latching or code quality (refused: the reader could never move it); two fields on one quality (refused); a checkpoint card value the quality does not allow (refused); a field that restates the whole description.
- **If wrong.** A field whose quality is never read keeps its first value; give the quality a rubric the reader can answer from the chat.

<a id="poses"></a>

## Poses and character layers

Topic `poses`.

Fields: `keypoints.format`, `keypoints.canvas`, `keypoints.points`, `roster[].sprites.poses`, `card.fields.layer`, `region.x`, `region.y`, `region.width`, `region.height`.

In Studio → Sprites → Poses, preview a skeleton, choose a member's default or direct it at the selected scene. The shipped library contains 40 original poses, including standing, sitting, kneeling, movement, fighting, casting, gestures and lying. Props name what the picture needs, such as a chair or staff. Render member in this pose is an explicit author preview; it needs your installed image setup. **Prepare story poses before play** renders, with their blink/talk frames, every pose the story names: each member's default pose and every pose a scene directs at them (not a scene that directs a sprite set, a hidden member, or the plain standing pose when the look has not changed), using the story's starting look. The stage then finds them ready at its first use instead of rendering during a turn. A new look rendered from the accepted base is refused when the face detector runs and finds no face in it (a render that drew the outfit without the head), and is rendered once more with a new seed.

On-demand pose work prepares the queued cast bodies before their blink/talk frames. A pose or look render that is still needed in play waits while SillyTavern is generating a reply, including the rest of a group round, and starts after it. Changing the stage or leaving the chat cancels obsolete setup, waits and renders. During bust/rig preparation, invalid landmark geometry gets one same-image correction attempt; hidden anatomy is refused rather than clamped into the crop.

A completed neutral pose body appears before expression work finishes, so a refused face edit leaves that pose visible with an error. Selecting a reference preserves its set's saved head box; an unconfigured reference uses the optional face detector when available. Generate waits until the head box for the selected character and reference is found. When the face detector answers, an expression, blink or mouth edit whose head box does not hold both eyes in its eye band (12–55% of its height) is refused before anything renders; if the character's accepted presentation head box does hold them, **Use <name>'s head box** replaces the saved box. Presentation expands the head-edit box into a wider, deeper bust crop to retain the chin, neck attachment, shoulders and upper torso; review this framing before accepting. The rig's neck pivot can use a visible collar opening, and shoulder anchors can sit on clothing or armor. Hidden joints and skin are never invented.

After the wizard creates a cast, **Next: prepare cast presentation** opens Sprites. Each wizard character card shows that character's accepted bust and base once presentation is accepted; until then it shows a placeholder, and **Prepare presentation** on the card opens Sprites too. Build a base candidate from installed card artwork using your configured Qwen 2.1 edit route and BiRefNet (the next seed is tried only when a candidate fails its checks; **Make another candidate** to compare), keep one, adjust its head box, then choose **Review selected base and bust**. Inspect both images before **Accept base and bust identity**. This explicit review records card/base/bust hashes and an accepted-source revision; a generated preview or a transparency check never approves identity. Cancel or a changed card/draft prevents acceptance. Replacing a source invalidates its derived looks.

**Reference views** (Sprites, optional) draw the accepted base three more ways round, three-quarter left and right, profile and back, with the same Qwen 2.1 route and BiRefNet; the accepted base and bust fill the full-body and front slots, six views in all. Choose **Draw reference views**, inspect all six, then **Accept all six views** or **Cancel reference views**. Nothing is saved before you accept. Accepting records the six files and a pack hash on the accepted source and starts a new source revision: every later sprite, pose, look and cast-scene key carries the pack hash, so changed looks render again. The pack is never required and never quality-approved by a check; no recipe uses the views as references yet.

The **Visual use-case routes and status** view joins edits/poses, bust/rig, prepared cast illustration and existing SDXL/background controls. In chat Illustrations, **Illustrate prepared cast** selects one or two installed non-narrator story members for a distinct Qwen 2.1 scene recipe using their accepted current-look identities. A look still being prepared (the outfit just changed) is waited for, up to four minutes; a missing, modified or still-pending identity is then refused, and the original outfit is not silently substituted. Changed-look derivatives retain source lineage but are not a fresh human quality approval. Live head uses a matching bust hash and rig for that look; an unprepared changed-look bust or rig uses transparent static fallback. The live head draws the current expression's own sprite (happy, angry, worried, or the pack's matching label) on the same rig, with a short crossfade, when that sprite lines up with the neutral one and changes nothing outside the head box; it is cut into eyes, lids and mouth the same way, and its blink and mouth frames (the neutral ones when the expression has none) are used only where their edges match. An expression without such a sprite keeps the neutral face with small brow and mouth accents, and the brow accent never moves the eyelids. **Changed-look bust and rig** (Sprites) lists every published look whose bust or rig is stale. **Rebuild bust and rig** crops the look with the expanded presentation framing around the accepted head box, asks the Sol vision model for face landmarks and fits a rig to them (eye openings, mouth, jaw, brows, head, shoulders and any loose hair locks, which then swing as the character moves); you see the bust and a moving preview, then **Accept rebuilt bust and rig** or **Cancel rebuild**. If the model refuses or is not offered, you can accept the bust alone and close shots stay static. When the optional face landmark server runs (`node scripts/local/landmarks.mjs start`, CPU only, anime-face-detector, MIT), the rebuild also reads the bust with that detector and compares its eyes, mouth and chin with the vision model's; an eye, the mouth or the chin more than 0.15 face widths away, swapped eyes, or a face oval far wider or narrower than the detected jaw shows a warning above the preview. The warning never blocks accepting; without the server the review notes that the landmarks were not cross-checked. A re-rendered look or a newly accepted source makes the rebuilt bust and rig stale again. A face or mark-only change (card fields on the `face` or `decal` layer) illustrates with the current outfit's artwork and describes those details in the scene prompt. Rig quality on real artwork has not been checked yet.

`poses.use` is an id or tag allowlist; absent means the whole library. `poses.custom` adds or overrides entries by id. Import the same JSON into This story or Every story on this install. A pose has `id`, `label`, `tags`, `framing` (full/thigh/close), `props`, a short pose `text`, and integer `version`. Its `keypoints` has `format: "openpose-body18"`, `canvas: [width,height]`, and exactly 18 `points`, each `[x,y]` or `null` for an occluded joint. Coordinates are in that canvas. Bump version when editing a pose. `when.keywords` makes a reply's matching keyword sticky until the scene changes. DWPose image import needs the approved estimator files already installed; selecting an entry in Model sources starts no download.

`roster[].sprites.pose` is the default id; `sprites.poses` limits that member's allowed ids. `effects.stage.<member>.pose` directs a pose. A direction can also specify `set`, `face`, `hidden` and per-member `framing`; global `stage.framing`, `spotlight` and the existing `cast` map still work. Priority is scene direction, sticky keyword, classifier pick, default. While a missing body renders, the stage chooses a same-look body with a shared tag, then standing, then a previous look in that pose, then the default/current sprite. Replies do not wait for this render. Missing faces use that body's expression fallback first.

Visual card fields declare `layer: "base" | "face" | "decal"` (base when omitted). Base fields change hair, outfit, equipment or age by rendering a whole body when its pose is next needed. While that body renders the stage shows the published look whose wording is closest (at least half the words shared per field, ignoring filler such as "the" or "over"), so a reworded outfit keeps its coat; with none that close it shows the original card art. `rebase: true` on a base field starts again from card art; use it for age/time skips. A face field edits only the head. A decal edits only `region: {x,y,width,height}` in normalized 0..1 coordinates, or the head when omitted. For example injury may be a decal and outfit a base field. A nonvisual field renders nothing. Swipes replay the applied look and pose; generated files stay cached.

Wizard tools: `setPoses`, `setMemberPoses`, `setPoseCard`, and `setCheckpointEffects` for the stage direction. The templates in `assets/workflows/poses` are story workflow bundles. `SO-Pose-P2` supplies the look base and a skeleton; `SO-Pose-P3` keeps the character reference and uses the pose text without a skeleton. Their image quality and render time have not been measured yet.
